mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate environment, as indicated by the FEDFUNDS series, reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5% and the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to higher wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.0%, the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in > 60% of such periods, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong underlying demand, which drives corporate revenue growth and positive equity returns; the interaction between these two series is necessary for the signal to be valid.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in > 50% of the periods when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month moving averages, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of rising industrial production (INDPRO), the S&P 500 tends to experience positive forward returns as higher manufacturing output signals robust economic growth and corporate earnings; this mechanism is most potent during the early stages of an expansion cycle.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in > 50% of periods during the early expansion cycle (as defined by INDPRO growth above 0.5% monthly and GDP growth above 2% annualized), or the Rank IC for the INDPRO signal in early expansion is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the year-over-year change of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals accelerating inflation, which typically leads to a monetary policy tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 2.5%, the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in > 50% of such periods, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which is a key driver of corporate revenue and profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average, the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in > 50% of the periods, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (the 2017 base) signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 100, the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in > 50% of such periods, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market, which drives corporate profit growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days; the joint condition is necessary for the signal to be valid.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in > 50% of the periods when PAYEMS is above its 3-month moving average and UNRATE is below its 3-month moving average, or the Rank IC for the joint signal is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
